doc.title: Ignacio Berroa interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Playing with a bass player who lacks the feel
summary: He supports the player, checks his ego, protects the music and offers advice later.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Yeah. So what if you’re on a gig and you have it, but the bass player doesn’t have it?

Well what I do, as a professional, as a musician, that’s a good point. Sometimes people that play either straight ahead or Afro-Cuban music in this case, and one of the musicians, the bass player doesn’t have it, immediately they get mad, they gave a face to the guy and that becomes a conflict. What I do as a professional, when I go to play with someone that doesn’t have it, I make the best that I can to make him look good so I don’t fight him, I join him. That’s me, Ignacio Berroa, as a human being and as a professional. Because that person is not doing that on purpose. He’s not doing that to bother me or to destroy the gig. He’s doing the best he can. So what I’m going to do is I’m going to be on his side. Let’s say, let’s be less humble. I’m going to come down to his level. I’m going to come down to his level, because what I always like to say and the most important thing for me is the music. That’s the only one that I try — that she cannot suffer, the music. I can take my ego and throw it off the window off the balcony, leave my ego at the coat check place. But when I go to the bandstand I’m going to do everything possible for the music not to suffer. So that’s what I do. I just come down to his level and then later on I give advice, “Hey man, listen, if you want to continue playing this style of music I think that you should check this, check that.” I give them advice. I give the guy or the band advice. But man, you know how many times I have seen it becomes a dogfight. And it isn’t pleasant. It’s simple as that, it’s unpleasant. If a guy comes to the stage to the bandstand and he doesn’t swing the way it’s supposed to swing, or he doesn’t know this, you know he’s not swinging, I have seen quite a few looks and the vibe and faces — what can I say? Once again, for me it is human nature.
